newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish pound takes a rest after recent volatility.
newsitem.headline: Irish pound takes a rest after recent volatility.

text.p: The Irish pound hovered above 2.5950 marks and 0.9200 sterling in afternoon trade on Wednesday as the market took a breather after the turbulence of recent days, dealers said.
"It's been remarkably quiet. The Irish pound has drifted up against the dollar and is straddling $1.5100 but overall, it's fairly quiet," one dealer said.
By 1600 GMT, the punt was at 0.9220 sterling and 2.5955 marks against 0.9183 and 2.5908 respectively at Tuesday's close.
Trading on the money markets was also quiet today, dealers said, with the one-month rate remaining steady around 6.13/6.25 percent.
But dealers and analysts said the Irish currency was not out of the woods yet and nervousness persisted in relation to the Irish pound with sellers seen emerging above 2.6000 marks.
"If we go over 2.60 I wouldn't be surprised to see some hedge funds stepping in and giving the Irish pound another smack," said Dominick Sutton, economist at Gandon Capital Markets.
"If they do that, the question is will the central bank move again. It's certainly not impossible. There's a lot of uncertainty out there and it's not a time to be overexposed," he said.

Dealers said Thursday could be quiet with several continental European markets closed for the Ascension Day holiday although some traders worried that the thin trading conditions could prompt volatility.
"Most of Europe was on holiday when we had the fun and games last week. The trouble with a holiday is it means thin markets which are easy to move," one dealer said.
Gandon's Sutton said the next few weeks could also prove nervy.

"My overall view for the next six weeks is that we are in for a very choppy period. There's so much on the horizon - the likelihood of an Irish election, a French election, all of that going on and the FOMC meeting on May 20," he said.
